research.abstract: Introduction The WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List identifies antibiotic-resistant bacteria posing a serious health threat. We aimed to analyse age-specific and region-specific burden trajectories and inequalities across countries with different socio-development levels for these pathogens. Methods We conducted a systematic analysis (1990-2021) using the Global Burden of Disease Study's Measuring Infectious Causes and Resistance Outcomes for Burden Estimation database, assessing trends and inequalities in mortality burden attributable to priority pathogens by age and region. Analyses included age-period-cohort modelling, average annual percentage change (AAPC) and health inequality metrics across countries stratified by sociodemographic index (SDI). Results Global mortality attributable to priority antibiotic-resistant pathogens rose from 5.47 to 6.12 per 100 000 in 1990-2021 (annual net drift: 0.086%). By age, mortality declined in under 5 but increased in the middle-aged and elderly (peaking at 40-44 and ≥95), primarily driven by carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella (AAPC 2.1%-2.4%) and Escherichia coli (AAPC 1.6%-2.2%). Mortality from multidrug-resistant tuberculosis rose across all ages, particularly in neonates (AAPC 7.4%, 95% CI 6.6% to 8.1%). Regionally, high-income Asia Pacific saw the steepest mortality decline (AAPC -2.5%, 95% CI -2.7% to -2.3%), while Eastern Europe exhibited the sharpest increase (AAPC 1.2%, 95% CI 0.2% to 2.2%), fueled by multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (AAPC 7.7%, 95% CI 6.0% to 9.5%), carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella (AAPC 3.5%, 95% CI 2.2% to 4.9%) and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (AAPC 3.1%, 95% CI 1.5% to 4.7%). Southern sub-Saharan Africa experienced a rise in fluoroquinolone-resistant Salmonella Typhi (AAPC 4.6%, 95% CI 2.5% to 6.8%). Over the 32-year period, the slope index of inequality in mortality burden of priority pathogens narrowed from -333.65 to -282.20, while the concentration index widened from -0.28 to -0.31. Conclusions The global mortality burden of priority antibiotic-resistant pathogens increased between 1990 and 2021, with age and regional disparities demanding targeted containment. Higher burden in low-SDI regions requires equitable healthcare resource allocation to combat antimicrobial resistance.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Bats are major reservoirs of emerging viruses, including severe acute respiratory syndrome‐related coronaviruses, yet they exhibit remarkable tolerance to viral infections with limited clinical manifestations‐a longstanding immunological paradox. Here, we generate a telomere‐to‐telomere (T2T) de novo genome assembly for Rhinolophus sinicus ( R. sinicus ), designated T2T‐RSC1.0 (2.14 Gb), comprising 17 fully anchored autosomes and both sex chromosomes. This gapless assembly resolves 129.19 Mb of previously unresolved regions (PURs) and enables annotation of 848 previously unannotated genes, including 131 protein‐coding genes and five pseudogenes on the 33.75 Mb Y chromosome. Using 2.12 × 10 5 newly identified single‐nucleotide polymorphisms within PURs, population genomic analyses resolve three major genetic groups and provide improved resolution of genome‐wide population structure. Comparative analyses further reveal population‐level associations between major histocompatibility complex polymorphism and viral diversity. Multi‐omics and functional analyses reveal a coordinated evolutionary remodeling of antiviral defense, antigen presentation, cytokine signaling, and inflammatory regulation in horseshoe bats. This study provides an unparalleled genomic resource for R. sinicus and establishes an integrated framework for investigating immune evolution, long‐term host–virus coexistence, and mammalian adaptive evolution.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Salmonella Typhimurium is a versatile foodborne pathogen with a broad ecological range, making it an ideal model to better understand pathogen adaptations that allow them to infect multiple hosts and persist across environments. Here, we analysed 595 genomes of S. Typhimurium representing three food animal sources (bovine, swine, and poultry) and one non‐food animal source (wild birds). We found that S. Typhimurium from food animal sources generally had a more open pangenome and harboured more antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). Notably, swine isolates exhibited the most open pangenome and the highest prevalence of ARGs, patterns that were associated with a greater presence of mobile genetic elements, particularly plasmids. Despite similar core genome sizes, S. Typhimurium from different sources displayed distinct patterns of positive selection in the core genome that varied in frequency and targeted functional categories. In contrast, although accessory genome sizes varied substantially across sources, the frequency of positive selection remained similar. Using machine learning, we identified source‐predictive genetic variants, many of which are associated with stress‐response functions. These findings suggest that gain and loss of accessory genes and positive selection acting on core genes support differential adaptation in S. Typhimurium, potentially contributing to its broad ecological range.

research.abstract: Estimating the effective sample size (ESS) is fundamental in Bayesian phylogenetic inference to account for autocorrelation in MCMC samples. While methods for continuous parameters are well established, the discrete and high-dimensional nature of treespace poses substantial challenges. In this paper, we introduce a new approach based on Conditional Clade Distributions (CCDs) to emulate MCMC chains with known ESS bounds. We compare existing tree ESS estimators with novel approaches that utilize CCDs as tractable tree distributions, as well as a new probabilistic estimator based on differences in clade frequencies between independent chains. Using our emulated chains from both simulated and real datasets, we assess estimators for their ability to recover the true ESS (accuracy), their insensitivity to the removal of autocorrelated samples from the chain (stability), and their tolerance to combining multiple chains together (robustness). We further examine how multimodality and poor inter-mode chain mixing can compromise the reliability of tree ESS estimates. These findings indicate that our new CCD-based estimators perform comparably to existing approaches with respect to accuracy, stability, and robustness. In contrast, the probabilistic estimator and two previously recommended methods incur prohibitive computational costs for long chains. Together, these results establish a new framework for evaluating tree ESS estimators using CCD-based emulated MCMC chains and demonstrate their performance and current limitations in practical phylogenetic analyses. The expanded suite of tree ESS estimators is available in the user-friendly TreeStat2 software package for BEAST 2.

research.abstract: Southeast Asia is home to 22 endemic raptors, and almost all are classified as “Endangered” or higher by the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN). The limited range and fragmented distribution of some Southeast Asian raptors from the genus Nisaetus hinder the characterization of these endangered birds. This study presents the mitochondrial sequences of the Pinsker’s Hawk-eagle ( Nisaetus pinskeri ) and Changeable Hawk-eagle ( Nisaetus cirrhatus ) and conducts a comparative mitogenome analysis across Accipitriformes. The partial mitogenome lengths of N. pinskeri and N. cirrhatus are 18,654 bp and 17,874 bp, with a GC content of 46.4% and 47.4%, respectively. An extra cytosine at position 174 of the nad3 gene was present in both mitogenomes, which was not previously observed in other Nisaetus species. Phylogenetic analysis recapitulated the topology of the order Accipitriformes. It showed that N. pinskeri and N. cirrhatus are closely related to each other and sister to the rest of the Nisaetus representatives. Moreover, the trees based on concatenated mitochondrial protein-coding genes were closer to the latest reported phylogenies than single-gene trees using conventional mitochondrial markers. The selection pressure analysis showed that all protein-coding genes experienced purifying selection, with the highest in atp8 and the lowest in cox1 . As the first report of the near-complete mitogenomes of these raptors, this study expands the available genomic resources for these understudied raptors and provides a foundation for future population genetic research.

research.abstract: Abstract Importance Severe maternal morbidity is increasingly driven by chronic conditions present before pregnancy, but existing obstetric comorbidity indices rely on clinician documentation and are not designed for preconception use. Objective To determine whether conditions represented in a patient-facing preconception assessment are associated with severe maternal morbidity comparably with clinician-derived indices. Design Retrospective cohort study of deliveries from 1992 to 2025; scores were derived from diagnoses recorded at least 280 days before delivery. Setting Two deidentified electronic health record databases covering an academic and public health system in San Francisco and 5 other University of California medical centers. Participants Birthing individuals aged 12 to 55 years at delivery with at least 10 clinical events recorded before conception. Exposures Preconception Medical Assessment (PreMA) score (range, 0-8) and the Bateman (range, 0-51) and Leonard (range, 0-281) obstetric comorbidity indices, modeled per 1-SD increase. Main Outcomes and Measures Severe maternal morbidity and nontransfusion severe maternal morbidity within 7 days of delivery, defined by Centers for Disease Control and Prevention indicators. Results Among 58,549 deliveries (21,427 in the San Francisco cohort [mean (SD) maternal age, 33.4 (5.7) years]; 37,122 in the statewide cohort [33.1 (5.4) years]), each 1-SD increase in PreMA score was associated with severe maternal morbidity in the San Francisco cohort (relative risk [RR], 1.23; 95% CI, 1.19-1.28), similar to the Bateman (RR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.22-1.29) and Leonard (RR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.23-1.30) indices; statewide findings were consistent. Severe maternal morbidity rose from 6.6% at a score of 0 to 9.0% at 1 to 3 and 17.8% at 4 or greater (statewide, 3.8%, 5.3%, and 14.5%). Associations persisted across racial, ethnic, and neighborhood deprivation subgroups. Cardiovascular conditions (RR, 3.08; 95% CI, 2.50-3.80) and diabetes (RR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.34-2.48) were most strongly associated with nontransfusion severe maternal morbidity. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study, higher scores on a patient-facing preconception assessment were associated with severe maternal morbidity, comparably with clinician-derived indices. Prospective studies are needed before scores are used clinically. Key Points Question Is a brief patient-completed preconception assessment associated with severe maternal morbidity? Findings In this study of 58,549 deliveries across two California health systems, each standard deviation increase in the electronic health record-derived Preconception Medical Assessment score was significantly associated with severe maternal morbidity, with a magnitude similar to two established clinician-facing comorbidity indices. Severe maternal morbidity ranged from 6.6% among deliveries with a score of 0 to 17.8% among those scoring 4 or greater. Meaning Conditions captured by this patient-completed assessment may identify candidates for preconception counseling and chronic disease optimization.

research.abstract: Abstract Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) remains a major global health threat, sustained by lengthy, multidrug treatment regimens that promote poor compliance and antibiotic resistance. The pathogen’s ability to evade clearance is facilitated in part by a transition to a nonreplicating, persistent state, a process thought to involve the abundant type II toxin-antitoxin (TA) systems. The Mtb chromosome encodes 11 MazEF TA systems whose MazF toxins are single-strand, sequence-specific endoribonucleases yet the precise RNA targets and physiological consequences of most remain unknown. Here we applied a specialized 5’-end RNA-seq approach to pinpoint the Mtb MazF-mt1 toxin recognition sequence and RNA target. MazF-mt1 specifically cleaves at U↓CCUU within the anti-Shine-Dalgarno (aSD) sequence, releasing it from the 3’ end of the 16S rRNA. Notably, the recently described MazF-mt11 toxin also targets the aSD for removal, cleaving at a different sequence 4 nts upstream of the MazF-mt1 site. Consistent with the essential role of the aSD in translation, both toxins rapidly inhibit new protein synthesis. This functional redundancy prompted us to mine Mtb transcriptomic datasets to compare how the two toxins respond to infection-relevant stresses. MazF-mt1 and MazF-mt11 are differentially regulated following exposure to diverse antibiotic and host-imposed stresses, with distinct temporal expression patterns. Thus, Mtb may coordinate transcription of these functionally redundant toxins to more precisely control the establishment and maintenance of nonreplicating persistence, thereby confounding pathogen clearance. Importance The ability of M. tuberculosis to resist immune-mediated clearance and antibiotic treatment is central to its success as a pathogen. Here, we identify the target of the endoribonuclease toxin MazF-mt1 as the anti-Shine-Dalgarno sequence near the 3’ end of 16S rRNA, cleavage of which causes rapid growth arrest and translation inhibition. Base-pairing between anti-Shine-Dalgarno/Shine-Dalgarno sequences is required for efficient ribosome recruitment and translation of most bacterial mRNAs. Because we previously reported that the MazF-mt11 toxin also cleaves the 16S rRNA 3’ end to remove the anti-Shine-Dalgarno sequence, MazF-mt1 expression phenocopies MazF-mt11. We further show that this toxin pair responds in contrasting ways to several first- and second-line antibiotics and a wide range of environmental stress conditions. Thus, M. tuberculosis encodes functionally redundant, ribosome-targeting toxins that are differentially deployed under stress, illuminating a potential mechanism to rapidly suppress translation and promote entry into a drug-tolerant, nonreplicating persistent state during infection.

research.abstract: Phylogenetic analyses of molecular evolution often require repeated manual preparation to reconcile taxa, annotate trees, execute models, and summarize results. These steps become increasingly time-consuming and difficult to standardize as the number of taxa, genes, and analytical hypotheses increases. We present HYphlow, an open-source graphical workflow developed in Python that integrates data preparation, trait-based foreground branch assignment, HyPhy execution, and structured result extraction within a single interface. HYphlow reconciles taxon labels across alignments, trees, and trait data; reconstructs ancestral states using parsimony and maximum likelihood; generates alternative foreground annotations; executes HyPhy analyses locally or through portable scripts for high-performance computing; and records analytical decisions and settings throughout the workflow. We evaluated HYphlow using simulations and two published datasets comprising cryptochrome analyses in pigeons and doves and visual opsin analyses in skinks. A name-similarity threshold of 80 reliably recovered simulated spelling variants, while consensus foreground assignment increased precision relative to parsimony or maximum likelihood alone (0.928 vs 0.891 and 0.907, respectively), with a corresponding reduction in recall (0.875 vs 0.921 and 0.918). In the empirical datasets, HYphlow reconciled taxon labels, reconstructed or reproduced foreground hypotheses derived using different approaches, and generated selection results consistent with the principal conclusions of the original studies. HYphlow therefore provides a reproducible framework for carrying comparative molecular evolutionary analyses from independently prepared sequence, phylogenetic, and trait data through branch assignment, model execution, and results summary while retaining researcher control over analytical decisions. HYphlow is freely available under the MIT licence from GitHub at: https://github.com/Schott-Lab/HYphlow.

research.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 has adapted continuously since 2019, yet no multi-parameter framework has characterized this trajectory across geographically distinct United States populations. We present a systematic 13-parameter analysis of 137,059 high-quality genomes from ten diverse US states across three phases: pre-vaccination (January-December 2020), early vaccination (January-June 2021), and sustained immune pressure (July 2021-December 2025), the latter dominated by the high-volume Delta period with an early-Omicron contribution. Approximately 5000 genomes were retrieved per state per phase from GISAID EpiCoV under stringent quality filters, and each phase dataset was partitioned into three subsets, giving 90 subsamples in total, to quantify subsampling stability. Parameters spanned genome-wide mutation rate, dN/dS and Ti/Tv, site-specific selection (HyPhy FUBAR), spike and ACE2 contact-residue profiling, insertion-deletion characterization, furin cleavage site evolution, N-linked glycosylation dynamics, lineage-mutation concordance, amino acid physicochemical shifts, and protein-wise dN/dS ranking and mutation load. Genome-wide mutation rate rose monotonically in all ten states, from 0.050% to 0.149%, and dN/dS rose from 0.611 to 1.103, crossing neutrality in nine of ten states by Phase 3. Amino acid mutation load increased 3.95-fold, from 9.12 to 36.03 substitutions per sequence, while Ti/Tv fell from 3.69 to 2.11. Spike position 142 was diversifying in all ten states in Phase 3, with positions 484, 452, and 478 recurring in 70, 60, and 60 percent of states. ORF8 followed a spike-then-collapse trajectory (dN/dS 3.43, 14.23, 1.01), consistent with progressive loss of function. The reproducibility of these effects across ten geographically distinct state populations establishes a state-level baseline for SARS-CoV-2 immune escape.

research.abstract: BACKGROUND: Long-read sequencing has revealed complex variations, such as gene conversions in immunologically critical PE/PPE gene families, yet their role in Mycobacterium tuberculosis host adaptation remains unclear. METHODS: We performed a comparative genomic analysis across a gradient of host-imposed selective pressure: chronic within-host infection, latent household transmission, and a 21-year clonal outbreak in Bern, Switzerland. RESULTS: We observed a constrained accumulation of mutational events across distinct epidemiological settings, with rates ranging from 0.36 to 0.81 events per genome per year. Under minimal host-imposed selection, the pathogen accumulated only small-scale variants (i.e., SNPs and indels). During the outbreak, however, the genetic diversity landscape shifted toward larger-scale variants, including recurrent gene conversions and structural variations. Notably, an early PPE19-to-PPE18 conversion emerged in the ancestral strain and was maintained across the entire lineage. In contrast, 86% of variants were transient singletons, with only a small proportion persisting under selection. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest a framework in which M. tuberculosis maintains genomic stability through purifying selection, while retaining the capacity to generate adaptive diversity through large-scale genetic rearrangements in immunologically relevant genomic features under intensified host pressure.

research.abstract: Abstract Tarsiers, an elusive family of primates found in Indonesia and the Philippines, sit at an essential point in primate evolution, with their divergence between that of Strepsirrhini (lemurs) and Simiiformes (monkeys and apes). Through homology searches, we have discovered that tarsiers carry the first known case in primates of a gene expansion of protein kinase R (PKR), a kinase involved in the response to viral infection. PKR was quadruplicated in the ancestor of tarsiers and has been maintained since then in all sequenced tarsier species. The extra copies lack the double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) binding domains necessary for detecting viral infection yet largely maintain the residues necessary for the kinase function that carries out PKR’s antiviral function. We show that three of the four PKR copies indeed maintain kinase activity, one of which appears to be resistant to the viral PKR antagonist K3 from vaccinia virus. Our analyses of site and branch-site positive selection reveal that the tarsier PKRs are under positive selection. We propose that these extra copies could serve as a diversification strategy to bypass viral inhibitors that bind PKR’s kinase domain, or they could alternatively serve as decoys that shield the canonical PKR from viral inhibition. This is the first instance of mammal PKR duplicates lacking dsRNA-binding domains and may highlight an innovation in an ancient, long-standing molecular arms race between viruses and a close relative of humans.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Mycobacterium abscessus (Mab) is an emerging opportunistic pathogen characterized by extensive intrinsic drug resistance, underscoring the need for precise genetic tools to define mechanisms of pathogenicity and persistence. The ORBIT ( o ligonucleotide-mediated recombineering followed by B xb1 integrase targeting) system developed by the Sassetti group (1) enables precise gene deletions but has primarily been optimized for Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Mycobacterium smegmatis . Although ORBIT has been used in Mab, here we describe an optimized ORBIT workflow for efficient gene deletion in Mab. We tested key parameters, including plasmid selection, oligonucleotide design, and recombineering conditions. We evaluated oligonucleotide length and purification to improve recovery of targeted mutants and established conditions that enabled reproducible deletion of multiple target genes. Our findings establish a robust and adaptable ORBIT protocol tailored to the genetic characteristics of Mab. This optimized workflow provides a practical framework for precise genetic manipulation and can facilitate functional studies of genes that contribute to Mab physiology, antimicrobial resistance, and pathogenesis. IMPORTANCE Mycobacterium abscessus causes the majority of intractable infections attributable to members of the M. abscessus complex: M. abscessus, M. massiliense and M. bolletii. M. abscessus infections most commonly present as chronic lung disease or as skin and soft tissue infections, and they are among the most difficult bacterial infections to eradicate, often persisting despite aggressive, prolonged treatment underscoring the need for reliable genetic tools to dissect the biology underlying pathogenesis. The ORBIT system enables precise, markerless gene deletion in mycobacteria, but its application to M. abscessus has been limited. Here we present an optimized ORBIT workflow tailored specifically to M. abscessus that will facilitate studies on the genes contributing to physiology and pathogenesis of this important pathogen.

research.abstract: Abstract Collagen is the most abundant protein in animals. Its thermal stability depends on its specific amino acid composition within the repeated Gly- Xaa -Y aa motifs forming the triple helix structure. Proline increases collagen rigidity, while serine enhances its elasticity—properties that contribute to collagen function and that vary with temperature. Although variation in collagen composition has been linked to temperature adaptation across evolutionary distinct taxa, its role within a species remains unclear. Here, we tested whether collagen genes across populations of the freshwater crustacean, Daphnia magna , show a signature of local adaptation to the ambient temperature. Analysing 39 collagen genes from 215 D. magna populations across three phylogeographic lineages spawning four continents, we found that animals from populations in warmer climates have higher proline and lower serine content in collagen—consistent with enhanced protein stability at higher temperatures. This variation was also associated with experimentally measured upper temperature tolerance. Parallel directional patterns of amino acid change appeared across genetically distinct lineages. Collagen genes also showed strong signatures of positive selection, comparable to that of immune-related genes, supporting a scenario of polygenic molecular role in adaptive responses. Our findings provide evidence of intraspecific molecular evolution in collagen amino acid composition driven by environmental temperature. Additionally, our study bridges macroevolutionary patterns with microevolutionary processes, posing the first intraspecific evidence that collagen genes can contribute to responses to environmental gradients at the molecular level, and thus, advancing our understanding of molecular adaptation of constrained structural proteins in an environmental context.

research.abstract: Abstract The Zygophyllaceae subfamily Zygophylloideae includes seven genera and around 180 species distributed worldwide particularly in arid areas where they show adaptations to drought including C 4 and CAM photosynthesis. Phylogenetic relationships of Zygophylloideae have been analysed in several studies using Sanger sequenced markers, but none have been able to resolve all deeper relationships between genera in the subfamily. Here, we use ion semi-conductor sequencing of chloroplast and nuclear ribosomal regions to analyse these relationships and assess why they have proved so challenging to resolve. We sequenced 39 chloroplast genes and nuclear ribosomal 18S, 5.8S, and 26S genes and internal transcribed spacers (ITS) for key species of Zygophyllum sensu stricto, Roepera, Tetraena, Fagonia , Zygophyllum stapffii and monotypic Augea capensis ; and Tribulus of the subfamily Tribuloideae as outgroup. We aligned these with data from published chloroplast genomes followed by phylogenetic analyses using Maximum Likelihood and Bayesian approaches, summarising phylogenetic results separately for non-coding introns and intergenic spacers, and for genes that are, or are not, involved in photosynthesis. We combined the chloroplast data with sequences of three highly variable noncoding chloroplast regions used in previous studies of greater numbers of taxa, and similarly the nuclear ribosomal data with more densely sampled ITS sequences and assessed whether adding such data resulted in improved support for consistent topologies. We used a chloroplast sequence matrix to infer a dated phylogeny. Adding data did not always improve phylogenetic resolution which was apparently impacted by non-informative variation in chloroplast photosynthesis related genes as well as by conflicting chloroplast and nuclear signals. Chloroplast genes not related to photosynthesis provide robust support for a topology that is consistent with independent data and may therefore represent a useful species tree hypothesis. The cause of the gene tree conflicts remains unclear: potential explanations include functional constraints in photosynthesis related genes and introgressive hybridization and/or incomplete lineage sorting during an ancient rapid divergence. Further testing will require a broader sampling of lineages with different photosynthetic modes and multiple informative, independent, and selectively neutral gene trees.

research.abstract: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV) remains the most economically devastating pathogen of the global swine industry, with frequent genetic recombination and continuous lineage replacement driving its rapid evolution. Hubei Province, a major swine-producing hub in central China, endures substantial PRRSV disease pressure, yet the current epidemiological and evolutionary landscape of circulating strains remains poorly characterized. In this study, 1478 clinical samples were collected from 12 prefecture-level cities between 2024 and 2025 and subjected to RT-PCR detection, ORF5 sequencing, virus isolation, and complete genome analysis. The detection rate among clinical samples was 26.32%, highest in nursery pigs (32.65%). research.abstract: DEG (Degradation of periplasmic proteins) proteases are ATP-independent serine endopeptidases found in bacteria, archaea, and eukaryotes including plants. They are considered to be key regulators of development and stress tolerance in plants. In this study, a comprehensive genome-wide analysis identified 19 serine protease-like DEG family proteins in potato (Solanum tuberosum L.), revealing their structural diversity, domain architecture, and regulatory potential. Physiochemical profiling showed a predominance of acidic isoelectric points (pI), variable protein lengths (169–1083 amino acids), and differential stability indices. Subcellular localization predicted most DEG proteases to reside in the chloroplast, with others distributed across cytoplasm, nucleus, mitochondria, and peroxisome. Domain analysis confirmed the universal presence of the trypsin domain, with varying numbers of PDZ domains and additional conserved motifs among paralogs. Evolutionary divergence analysis of StDEG genes and their orthologs from six Solanaceae species as well as Arabidopsis thaliana, Oryza sativa, and Zea mays revealed dN/dS ratios below one for all orthologous pairs, suggesting that StDEG genes have evolved under strong purifying selection and remained highly conserved throughout plant evolution. Gene ontology annotations linked DEG proteases to key biological functions including PSII repair, photoinhibition, and chloroplast organization, alongside protein catabolism and light stimulus response. Promoter analysis revealed an abundance of cis-regulatory elements (CREs), particularly light-responsive motifs, along with hormone and stress-related elements such as ABRE, ARE, and MBS. Expression profiling across eight developmental tissues demonstrated tissue-specific expression patterns, with strong transcript accumulation of selected DEG members in senescent leaf, stolon, shoot apex, and tuber. Interestingly, several splice variants showed unique expression dynamics, including stage-specific and stress-induced activation. Upon exposure to abiotic and hormonal cues, 16 DEG proteases displayed significant transcriptional modulation, particularly under light, ABA, and Zeatin treatments, with notable fold changes reaching up to 26-fold in certain variants. These findings highlight the functional versatility of DEG proteases in potato development and stress adaptation, especially their responsiveness to light and hormonal stimuli. The characterization of these proteases paves the way for future studies on their roles in crop resilience and genome editing applications.

research.abstract: Understanding the mechanisms facilitating the repeated evolution of traits is a core question in evolutionary biology. While repeated evolution has been observed across many systems, behavioral phenotypes have been less well studied than morphological traits. Migration is a behavioral adaptation to seasonality that has evolved independently in many animals, and repeated gains and losses of migratory behavior have been especially prevalent throughout the diversification of birds. While migratory traits are heritable in many taxa and candidate genes underlying intraspecific variation in migratory behavior have been identified, whether similar genetic changes are responsible for the repeated evolution of migration remains poorly understood. We used a phylogenomic approach to investigate the relationship between variation in candidate genes and migratory propensity across nearly all species in the parulid warbler radiation (n = 101), a group of songbirds in which migratory behavior has been lost and gained multiple times. Comparisons of candidate gene tree topologies to the parulid warbler species tree revealed cases of discordance, though these were explained by differences in the number of phylogenetically informative sites among genes rather than by elevated genetic similarity among species sharing migratory strategies. Testing models of coding sequence evolution identified sites with elevated dN/dS in five candidate genes, suggestive of positive selection; however, variation at these sites showed no clear association with migratory strategy, nor did we detect recurrent selection across lineages where transitions in migratory behavior most likely occurred. Together, these results contradict the hypothesis that selection on shared variation (ancestral polymorphisms or introgressed alleles) facilitated the repeated evolution of migration in this clade.

research.abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are key defence molecules of the innate immune system. Understanding the origins of AMPs can help to explain how immune systems acquire novelty and vary in their defence capacities. However, AMPs evolve rapidly, and so the origins of similar AMPs across organisms is often unclear. Furthermore, false negatives due to low search sensitivity are common and can hinder conaident annotations about true absences. As a result, understanding whether similar AMP genes found in diverse organisms represent ancestral molecules or evolutionary novelties has been challenging. Here, we present evidence of horizontal gene transfer (HGT) of the antifungal peptide gene Drosomycin across insects. We show that in Diptera, the presence of Drosomycin is restricted to the Drosophila Melanogaster species group and additionally the distant relative Drosophila busckii. We go on to recover Drosomycin genes in cockroaches (Blattodea), mantises (Mantodea), katydids (Orthoptera), beetles (Coleoptera), parasitic wasps (Hymenoptera), and a recently acquired and pseudogenized Drosomycin locus in Liposcelis booklice (Psocodea), but not other insects. Explaining this diversity through shared ancestry requires at least 60 independent loss events, or just nine HGT events. Previous studies have suggested that similar AMPs found across divergent species realect conservation from a common ancestor, or due to their small size, that they arose via convergent evolution. Our aindings suggest horizontal gene transfer can be responsible for the presence of some AMP genes scattered across the tree of life. By presenting a mechanism through which immune systems can acquire novelty, our study also suggests a possible explanation for certain lineage-speciaic defence competencies against infectious disease. While loss of AMP genes is well-documented, here we suggest gain of AMPs can occur just as suddenly.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing global public health threat. The water bodies act as both reservoirs and medium for dissemination of AMR. Coastal water driven by anthropogenic effects accumulate antibiotics, heavy metals, microplastics, and disinfectants which act as stressors, increasing the overall AMR. Therefore, it is necessary to understand the AMR entities and its transmission in coastal water bodies. Methods and Results Mumbai, mirroring most cosmopolitan cities of the world, was used as a model to understand how rapid urbanization disseminate AMR in coastal waters of the Arabian Sea and can pose substantial risk to human health. Bacteria isolated from coastal waters were screened and found to be multi-drug resistant. Several isolates carried multiple plasmids of high molecular weight (>10 kb). Plasmid sequencing and analysis using various bioinformatic tools identified plasmid replicons like IncFIA, IncFII, rep7a and repUS43. Analysis showed a high burden of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) conferring resistance to antibiotic classes such as monobactams (bla TEM-116 ), carbapenems (bla NDM-5 ), vancomycin ( vanA ), disinfectants and antiseptics ( qacG ). Additionally, clinically relevant mecA and mecR1 associated with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus sp., rpsL associated with streptomycin resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis and the colistin-resistance genes mcr-10 . 1 and mcr-10 . 4 were also detected. We also report for the first-time presence of a plasmid-borne mupB gene in coastal waters, that confers high resistance to mupirocin. Conclusions Despite the moderate sample size, the presence of diverse plasmid replicons and clinically important ARGs suggests urban coastal environment as a potent reservoir of AMR, with potential for global transmission through active waterway trade and transport.

research.abstract: Abstract The study of complex disorders is limited by the lack of structured data sets that integrate genetic association signals with rich functional annotations. While genome-wide association studies (GWAS) provide large collections of associated variants, these are heterogeneous, study-dependent, and not directly suitable for machine learning applications. Although frameworks such as Combined Annotation Dependent Depletion (CADD) offer comprehensive variant-level features, there is no standardised procedure to construct curated, balanced, and reproducible data sets for the systematic study of complex traits. We introduce a scalable and reproducible pipeline for generating CADD-annotated variant data sets associated with complex disorders defined via Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO) terms. The pipeline integrates GWAS summary statistics, genome mapping, chromosome-stratified negative sampling, and large-scale annotation, while addressing class imbalance and feature redundancy. The resulting data sets provide curated, balanced, and annotation-rich representations of variant–trait associations, suitable for statistical learning, systematic model evaluation and comparison, and analysis of functional annotation contributions and interactions.

research.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis remains the leading cause of death from a single infectious pathogen globally despite decades of effective chemotherapy. In 2024, an estimated 10·7 million people developed tuberculosis, including approximately 620 000 people living with HIV (PLHIV), and tuberculosis caused an estimated 1·23 million deaths overall, including approximately 150 000 deaths among PLHIV. Men accounted for more than half of the cases, and children represented a substantial burden, reflecting ongoing transmission and diagnostic gaps. Approximately a quarter of the world's population has been infected with M tuberculosis, with immunological evidence of previous or current infection. This population includes groups at increased risk of progression to tuberculosis disease, particularly those with recent infection, HIV, undernutrition, young age, or other clinical and social vulnerabilities. Following 3 years of COVID-19-related setbacks, global tuberculosis incidence declined modestly (1%) from 2023 to 2024 but remains higher than in 2020 and far off-track to meet the 2025 WHO End TB Strategy milestones. Case detection improved to 8·3 million notifications (78% of estimated incident cases), supported by expanded molecular diagnostics; however, prevalence surveys continue to reveal substantial proportions of bacteriologically confirmed but asymptomatic tuberculosis, highlighting persistent transmission and missed diagnoses. 30 high-burden countries accounted for 87% of cases, led by India, Indonesia, the Philippines, China, Pakistan, Nigeria, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Bangladesh. M tuberculosis-HIV co-infection remains a major driver of mortality in sub-Saharan Africa. Drug-resistant tuberculosis threatens progress: of 390 000 estimated multidrug-resistant or rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis cases in 2024, only 42% initiated treatment, although treatment success improved to 71%. Tuberculosis-preventive treatment reached 5·3 million people, including 58% of PLHIV and 25% of eligible household contacts, well below global targets. Persistent undernutrition, poverty, HIV, diabetes, smoking, alcohol use, air pollution, migration, and conflict continue to shape tuberculosis epidemiology. With financing at only 27% of global targets, accelerated prevention, proactive case finding, social protection, and sustained political commitment are essential to eliminate tuberculosis.

research.abstract: In young animals, oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) in the CNS efficiently differentiate into myelinating oligodendrocytes (OLs), whereas ageing reduces this capacity, impairing remyelination following demyelinating injury and adaptive myelination involved in learning. To identify factors that restore resilience in aged OPCs, we developed gSWITCH ( https://altoslabs.shinyapps.io/gSWITCH/ , https://github.com/Tanay-math/gSWITCH ), a computational pipeline that captures dynamic gene-expression patterns to identify ‘switch’ genes during lineage progression and ordered biological transitions, including time-series experiments. gSWITCH identified OPC-characteristic switch genes, which we compared between young and aged OPCs to determine whether their regulation is altered with ageing. This revealed several transcription factors with reduced expression in aged OPCs. Transcription-factor binding-site enrichment highlighted Bcl11a as a potential master-regulator of multiple switch genes. Bcl11a inhibition reduced OPC differentiation into OLs, whereas its overexpression in aged OPCs significantly enhanced OL differentiation without affecting proliferation. In aged mice subjected to demyelination injury in spinal cord white matter, Bcl11a overexpression increased OPC differentiation within lesions. We found that Bcl11a has undergone pervasive purifying selection throughout vertebrate evolution, preserving its amino acid sequence by eliminating deleterious mutations. Our study shows that reversing the age-related decline of this evolutionarily conserved factor in aged OPCs restores their impaired capacity for differentiation.

research.abstract: SUMMARY Germline-targeting or lineage-based vaccine strategies are being used to induce HIV broadly neutralizing antibody (bnAb) responses. These strategies assume that genetically diverse individuals respond similarly to the same immunogen by mobilizing comparable germline precursors, although outcomes vary across bnAb epitopes. Here we explored this premise using a simian-HIV infection model in rhesus macaques. Antigen-unbiased Env-reactive B-cell populations were profiled, followed by systematic analysis of antibody function and B-cell receptor (BCR) genetics. We find that while global Env-reactive B-cell response profiles and antibody functional properties are similar across individuals, underlying BCR genetics are diverse, particularly among non-bnAbs. These results indicate that functional convergence of Env-reactive antibody responses does not necessarily require genetic convergence and suggest that specific germline-targeting may not be an absolute prerequisite for successful vaccine design. These findings support an epitope-focused framework in which bnAb epitopes are engineered to enhance population-level immunogenicity, with potential applicability to other challenging pathogens.

research.abstract: Abstract Background The vaginal microbiome is a key determinant of women’s health, with Lactobacillus -dominant communities protecting against bacterial vaginosis ( BV ) and related adverse outcomes. Dysbiosis involves a decline in lactobacilli and overgrowth of anaerobes, with Gardnerella species central to initiating polymicrobial aggregates. However, the genetic determinants of community assembly, biofilm formation, and interspecies interactions remain poorly understood. This study investigated the genomic and functional basis of these traits using an integrated multi-omics approach. Results Long-read whole-genome sequencing of clinical Gardnerella isolates yielded closed genomes and revealed a pangenomic split correlating with high-versus low-biofilm phenotypes, linked to clade-specific genomic islands and allelic variants. Functional gene modules within these regions distinguished G. vaginalis from G. piotii , contributing to nutrient acquisition, cell wall metabolism, and colonization. Integrated 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and proteomics of all pairwise dual-species co-cultures of five key vaginal bacteria showed that G. vaginalis and L. iners acted as dominant ecological drivers, outcompeting neighbors and triggering asymmetric proteomic remodeling. Differential expression of a gene within a putative operon encoding a conserved type II secretion/Tad pilus system, revealed by integrating the pangenome with the proteome, implicated this system in interspecies interactions. AI-based structural predictions of the complex suggested isoform-specific differences in protein folding between G. vaginalis and G. piotii . In parallel, metagenomic analysis of 93 women showed the operon was more abundant in BV samples than in healthy controls, linking it to dysbiosis. Integrated metabolomics further identified a methyl-β-carboline compound elevated in Prevotella bivia -containing co-cultures that selectively inhibited G. vaginalis and P. bivia while sparing L. crispatus . Several dipeptides influenced growth and biofilm formation of vaginal microbes, and methyl-β-carboline and sphingosine additionally inhibited multidrug-resistant pathogens, suggesting new strategies for managing polymicrobial infections. Conclusions This work links Gardnerella genomic features to virulence-associated phenotypes and demonstrates how interspecies interactions shape community dynamics and antimicrobial metabolite production. The findings support a model in which biofilm capacity is genetically encoded within an accessory genome, deployed through tailored proteomic responses, and modulated by an interaction-specific metabolic landscape, providing a foundation for identifying bioactive molecules and developing diagnostics and targeted therapeutics to restore and maintain vaginal health. Highlights Long-read whole-genome sequencing of clinical Gardnerella isolates yielded closed ge-nomes and linked high-versus low-biofilm phenotypes to clade-specific genomic islands and allelic variants. Integrated 16S rRNA gene sequencing, proteomics, and metabolomics of all pairwise du-al-species co-cultures showed that Gardnerella vaginalis and Lactobacillus iners outcompete neighboring species and trigger asymmetric proteomic remodeling, identifying them as dominant ecological drivers of dysbiosis. AI-predicted structural variation in a conserved type II secretion/Tad pilus system, sup-ported by metagenomic cohort analysis of 93 women, distinguished healthy from dysbiotic states and highlights a candidate BV biomarker. Integrated metabolomics identified a methyl-β-carboline elevated in Prevotella bivia -containing co-cultures that selectively inhibits G. vaginalis and P. bivia while sparing L. crispatus , offering a narrow-spectrum therapeutic lead. Metabolites including several dipeptides modulated growth and biofilm of vaginal mi-crobes and multidrug-resistant pathogens, suggesting new strategies for managing polymicrobial infections

research.abstract: Mitochondrial genomes (mitogenomes) are no longer considered entities solely responsible for cellular bioenergetics, but as dynamic, multifaceted, and synchronized systems that integrate genome architecture, evolutionary processes, and organismal physiology. The present review summarizes the contemporary understanding of mitogenome organization and its diversity, evolution, and associated functions across eukaryotic life, with emphasis on mitonuclear co-evolution and relevance to human health. Moreover, the conserved and lineage-specific characteristics of mitogenome architecture, including its genetic content, topology, and regulatory elements, and their roles in governing the precise replication and transcription of the mitogenome are also comprehensively discussed. Additionally, the review explores the role of evolutionary dynamics, with emphasis on mutation-rate heterogeneity, recombination dynamics, gene rearrangements, and the interaction between mutation, natural selection, and genetic drift in shaping mitochondrial genome diversity and evolutionary trajectories. Comparative approaches have revealed extensive diversity in mitogenome structural organization and composition, which are closely associated with life-history traits of organisms, including metabolic rate, longevity, and reproductive characteristics. Notably, at the functional level, the variability potential of a mitogenome significantly influences oxidative phosphorylation efficiency, reactive oxygen species generation, and the orchestration of cellular signaling cascades. Fundamental to these processes is the existence of coordinated mitonuclear interrelationships, wherein coevolution between mitochondrial and nuclear-encoded genes safeguards bioenergetic functional integrity, whereas disruptions in this coordination may lead to reduced cellular fitness and progression of several diseases. Particularly in humans, mutations in mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and heteroplasmy significantly contribute to the development of primary mitochondrial disorders and are increasingly implicated in other complex disease etiologies, including neurodegeneration, metabolic syndromes, and cancer. The paper also summarizes the phylogenetic utility of mitogenomes in the genomic era, accentuating the need to employ integrative approaches that combine mitochondrial and nuclear data. Lastly, the role of emerging technological platforms, including long-read sequencing and multi-omics, is also discussed, since these approaches are expected to transform the current landscape of mitogenome research. Altogether, the manuscript positions mitogenomes as indispensable entities bridging the gaps between evolutionary histories, physiological functions, and personalized precision medicine.

research.abstract: Background Toll-like receptor genes have been extensively researched for their role in the susceptibility to pulmonary tuberculosis across different populations. This study aimed to elucidate the association of TLR2 T597C, TLR4 A896G, and TLR9 G1174A gene polymorphisms with the risk of developing pulmonary tuberculosis. Methods A total of 306 samples – 153 patients with pulmonary tuberculosis and 153 age- and sex-matched healthy controls were selected using a consecutive sampling technique. Clinical and biochemical variables were measured to assess the associated risk factors. Deoxyribonucleic acid was isolated from blood samples, and the TLR2 , TLR4, and TLR9 genotypes were identified using polymerase chain reaction–restriction fragment length polymorphism and analyzed by agarose gel electrophoresis. Results Our analysis showed that the TLR2 -CC genotype (OR = 3.82; 95% CI = 1.79–8.16; P < 0.001) and C allele (OR=2.12; 95%CI: 1.42–3.10; P < 0.001), the TLR4 -GG genotype (OR=3.18; 95%CI: 1.71–5.92; P < 0.001) and G allele (OR=2.25; 95%CI: 1.61–3.14; P < 0.001), and the TLR9 -AA genotype (OR=2.00; 95%CI: 1.09–3.68; P = 0.025) and A allele (OR=1.60; 95%CI: 1.15–2.21; P < 0.001) is significantly associated in patients than in controls, suggesting their potential role as genetic risk factors for the development of pulmonary tuberculosis. Combined genotype analysis revealed that individuals carrying all three risk genotypes (CC-GG-AA) significantly associated with increased PTB risk. Multivariable analysis showed that HIV co-infection and malnutrition were independent predictors of pulmonary tuberculosis. Conclusion The TLR2 T597C gene of the CC genotype and the C allele, the TLR4 A896G genes of the GG genotype and the G allele, and the TLR9 G1174A genes of the AA genotype and the A allele are associated with increased risk of pulmonary tuberculosis among the Ethiopian patients under study.

research.abstract: Abstract High-throughput sequencing has transformed RNA virus discovery, producing vast datasets that often contain unexplored sequences of known and novel viruses across diverse sample types. Large-scale reconstruction of viral genomes within specific taxonomic groups remains a lengthy, labor-intensive process constrained by fragmented assemblies, heterogeneous workflows, and the limitations of percent identity cut-offs for taxonomic placement. Here, we focused on Tobamovirus (family Virgaviridae ), a genus that contains important emerging plant pathogens. Tobamoviruses are detectable in diverse environmental matrices and are thus expected to be present across a range of datasets. We mined global short-read datasets to uncover hidden tobamovirus diversity, combining expert curation with supervised machine learning to streamline the discovery of novel tobamoviruses. Using the Serratus PalmID tool, we first identified 253 candidate datasets that are most likely to contain novel tobamoviruses. We developed a reproducible Snakemake pipeline for quality control, de novo assembly, similarity searches, and preliminary taxonomic assignment, yielding 510 candidate tobamovirus contigs across 131 datasets. Following manual curation, we confirmed 228 tobamoviral contigs from 23 datasets based on BLAST similarity searches, coding sequence content, genome organization, and assessment of potential misassemblies. To expedite the curation process, we built a two-stage machine learning classifier of tobamoviral contigs. Based on alignment-derived features and sequence properties, each ORF is first scored to determine whether it is tobamoviral. ORF-level predictions are then merged into contig-level classification using stacked generalization. Through clustering and phylogenetic analyses, we identified at least 32 putative novel tobamoviruses in datasets derived from freshwater, wastewater, plants, animal gut, and soil. Most were placed within established Tobamovirus subclades, whereas a few highly divergent sequences formed distinct basal branches related to recently identified soil-associated sequences classified as Virgaviridae sp. These findings highlight the value of aquatic and wastewater systems for expanding our understanding of tobamoviral diversity and demonstrate how data mining and targeted curation can substantially expand recognized diversity within the genus. The workflow is readily adaptable to other viral taxa and supports continuous discovery as public datasets grow.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Biological function is often inferred from sequence conservation or structural similarity. However, many viral RNAs maintain regulatory functions despite extensive diversification of both sequence and structures. Using arenavirus intergenic regions (IGRs) as a model system, we investigated what level of RNA organization remains conserved when these conventional sequence-structure-function relationships break down. Combining cryogenic OrbiSIMS guided RNA structure determination with graph theory-based analysis of fifty-eight IGRs across phylogenetically diverse arenaviruses, we discovered that IGR topology, defined by the connectivity and relative integration of individual stem-loop elements, is consistently arranged around a highly connected helical core that persists across divergent IGR folds. Quantitative centrality analyses further revealed that topologically peripheral stem-loops are comparatively sparse and variable across the phylogenetic classes. Investigation of the functional consequence of the peripheral elements in Golden Gate virus (a reptile arenavirus) S-IGR revealed selective association with interferon-induced and antiviral RNA-binding proteins in human host cells infected with recombinant Lymphocytic Choriomeningitis virus (a distantly related human arenavirus). Taken together, these findings identify graph-defined topology as a recurrent organisational feature among divergent arenavirus IGRs that is not captured by sequence identity or global RNA-structure similarity. The data are consistent with a model in which a topologically central helical organisation may be associated with conserved regulatory capacity, whereas structurally variable peripheral elements may contribute to lineage- or segment-specific host-factor interaction profiles.

research.abstract: Computing phylogenetic likelihoods becomes challenging when the continuous-time Markov chain has a large state space. At each branch, pruning algorithms require terms of the form $e^{Q t}\cdot B$, where $Q$ is an $S \times S$ rate matrix (e.g., for $S$ states), $t$ is a branch length, and the columns of matrix $B$ (e.g., $B \in \mathbb{R}_{+}^{S \times L}$) are partial-likelihood vectors for $L$ site patterns. Many implementations calculate the dense transition matrix $P(t)=e^{Q t}$ via eigendecomposition and multiply it by $B$. This strategy is efficient for small state spaces, but it can be inefficient for large sparse rate matrices because forming $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices destroys sparsity and its cost may not be well amortized when $L$ is small. We implement an alternative likelihood kernel based on the Al-Mohy and Higham (2011) algorithm for computing the action of the matrix exponential directly, avoiding explicit construction of $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices. The resulting method takes full advantage of the sparsity of $Q$. We implement this method as a CPU-based extension to the BEAGLE library and evaluate it on two large-state molecular models: a Markov-modulated codon model of heterotachy with $M$ selective regimes and $61\cdot M$ possible states, and a codon-pair model of interlocus gene conversion between two paralogs with $61^2=3\,721$ possible states. Our results characterize when action-based likelihood computation improves performance over calculating $e^{Q t}$ directly. We show that this method enables fast, scalable inference for complex models, removing a key computational barrier to the study of evolution with large state space models.

India, a high- tuberculosis burden country, faces growing challenges of delayed diagnosis, treatment and drug-resistant tuberculosis, particularly in extrapulmonary forms. This study evaluated early clinical response to therapy and identified factors associated with rifampicin resistance among patients with EPTB. A prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary care centre in central India between 2018 and 2024. A total of 532 patients with microbiologically confirmed EPTB, based on the Xpert MTB/RIF assay, were included. The study collected baseline demographic, clinical, and laboratory data. Clinical response at 8 weeks was assessed using standardized criteria. Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified factors associated with slow clinical response and rifampicin resistance. A total of 5,764 presumptive EPTB samples were tested using the Xpert MTB/RIF assay. Among these, 532 patients had confirmed EPTB. Rifampicin resistance was detected in 36 patients (6.7%), while 496 patients had rifampicin-sensitive disease and were included in the response analysis. Among these patients, 113 (22.8%) demonstrated slow clinical response. Slow response showed independent association with HIV co-infection, diabetes mellitus, malnutrition, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, prolonged symptom duration, and non-lymph node disease, particularly abdominal and genitourinary tuberculosis. Socioeconomic factors, such as rural residence and lower educational status, also showed independent association. Elevated inflammatory markers, including erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein, showed independent association with slow clinical response. Rifampicin resistance showed independent association with previous tuberculosis, HIV infection, male sex, and disseminated disease. A significant overlap existed between delayed clinical response and drug resistance, as rifampicin resistance occurred more frequently among slow responders than among responders (12.3% vs. 4.1%, p = 0.002). Nearly one-quarter of patients with EPTB demonstrated delayed clinical response at 8 weeks. Both host-related and disease-related factors showed association with treatment response, while rifampicin resistance showed strong association with prior tuberculosis and immunosuppression. The overlap between slow clinical response and drug resistance highlighted the importance of early molecular diagnostics and targeted clinical monitoring in high-risk patients.

research.abstract: Abstract Pulmonary tuberculosis remains one of the most prevalent and threatening infectious diseases. Classical anti-tubercular therapy targets essential enzymes of the pathogen Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), thereby suppressing bacterial growth. However, the emergence of drug-resistant strains necessitates alternative therapeutic approaches. Virulence inhibition is a promising strategy that blocks Mtb virulence factors required for survival within host cells. We previously identified a hit compound, BTP15, which protected fibroblasts and THP-1 macrophages from Mtb-induced cell death ex vivo by blocking phagosomal escape through inhibition of the mycobacterial histidine kinase MprB. Due to poor pharmacokinetics, the structure of BTP15 was optimized. New benzothiophene derivatives were screened for MprB inhibition, microsomal stability, toxicity, and ex vivo efficacy in THP-1 and MRC-5 cells. The lead compound, 7a, exhibited favorable pharmacokinetic parameters, showed no toxicity in mice at 250 mg/kg, and prevented Mtb dissemination in an acute mouse model of tuberculosis.

research.abstract: Phylogenetic trees are hybrid objects: branch lengths vary continuously, while topologies change discretely through edge contractions and expansions. Billera-Holmes-Vogtmann (BHV) tree space provides a canonical geometry for this structure, representing each resolved topology as a Euclidean orthant and topological changes as motion across shared lower-dimensional boundaries. We introduce PhylaFlow, a hybrid flow-matching model that learns posterior-basin transport in BHV tree space. PhylaFlow is trained on BHV geodesic paths from random starting trees to short-run posterior samples, coupling continuous branch-length motion within orthants with learned boundary events and discrete topology transitions. We evaluate the learned geometry operationally: if the flow reaches posterior-relevant regions, finite-budget Bayesian refinement initialized from, or guided by, its terminal trees should recover posterior-supported topologies more efficiently. Across DS1-DS8 phylogenetic posterior benchmarks, PhylaFlow substantially reduces initial Tree-KL relative to classical initializers. After finite-budget MrBayes refinement, direct PhylaFlow improves early and intermediate topology-recovery trajectories on most datasets, while split-guided PhylaFlow-MCMC obtains the strongest hard-case results. The best PhylaFlow variant outperforms short-warmup on seven of eight datasets and PhyloGFN on five of eight under the same refinement budget. In a joint sequence-conditioned experiment, sequence embeddings steer posterior split recovery, although exact posterior topology recovery remains preliminary. These results show that hybrid flow matching can learn actionable transport in BHV tree space and provide a geometry-aware proposal mechanism for Bayesian phylogenetic inference.

research.abstract: Abstract Background High temperature severely limits tomato reproductive development and yield, particularly in tropical production systems. Pollen viability and fruit set are commonly used as indicators of reproductive heat tolerance, but much of the supporting evidence has been obtained under controlled conditions. Their relevance to breeding under variable open-field environments remains less clear. This study investigated reproductive performance and its genetic basis under open-field heat stress using a multi-parent advanced generation inter-cross (MAGIC) population. Results We developed a MAGIC population from eight Solanum lycopersicum parents combining heat tolerance and multiple disease resistances and evaluated 262 F 5:6 lines under natural open-field heat stress. Flower number showed the highest heritability (0.64), followed by pollen viability (0.56), fruit number (0.48), and days to flowering (0.25), whereas fruit set showed negligible heritability (<0.01). Despite its moderate heritability, pollen viability was only weakly correlated with fruit set ( r = 0.22). In contrast, fruit number was strongly correlated with fruit set ( r = 0.86), supporting fruit number as a practical selection criterion for reproductive performance under open-field heat stress. Restriction enzyme-associated DNA sequencing generated 16,350 high-quality SNPs for genome-wide association analysis, which identified multiple QTLs for reproductive traits, several overlapping previously reported loci. A region on chromosome 6 at approximately 31–33 Mb was particularly notable because it was associated with multiple reproductive traits and coincided with a previously reported heat-responsive QTL region. Candidate-gene analysis highlighted floral developmental regulation, represented by positional candidates SlAGO7 , ENO , and SlWUS , and cellular and protein homeostasis, supported by direct candidates including MON1, ECM29, and ubiquitin-related genes. Conclusions Selection criteria established under controlled environments may not fully predict reproductive performance under open-field heat stress. Fruit number provides an integrative and moderately heritable indicator of realized reproductive success under field conditions. The identified QTLs and candidate genes provide targets for validation and development of heat-tolerant tomatoes adapted to tropical open-field production.

research.abstract: Mycobacterium abscessus (Mab) is a rapidly growing non-tuberculous mycobacterium that causes opportunistic infections and exhibits extensive intrinsic antibiotic resistance. The proline-glutamate (PE) and proline-proline-glutamate (PPE) protein families are mycobacteria-specific virulence factors implicated in immune modulation, antigenic variation, and persistence. While Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) harbors approximately 170 PE/PPE members, the repertoire of PE/PPE genes in Mab remains largely uncharacterized. Here, we performed a genome-wide survey of PE/PPE genes in Mab ATCC 19,977 and identified 18 candidate family members, representing a relatively small fraction of the genome compared with slow-growing mycobacteria. Most predicted proteins harbor canonical PE or PPE domains and display acidic physicochemical properties. Phylogenetic analysis resolved the proteins into three subfamilies: PE, PPE, and PE-PPE, revealing moderate structural diversity but limited family expansion. Motif and gene structure analyses supported the evolutionary conservation. Notably, no PE_polymorphic GC-rich repetitive sequence (PE_PGRS) or PPE_major polymorphic tandem repeat (PPE_MPTR) members were detected, suggesting lineage-specific genomic reduction relative to other pathogenic mycobacteria. AlphaFold predictions revealed conserved N-terminal folds and variable C-terminal regions, which may contribute to functional diversification. Subcellular localization predictions indicated that most proteins are extracellular. Synteny analysis revealed no detectable collinearity among these genes. Transcriptomic analyses revealed condition-dependent expression of PE/PPE genes during amoeba and macrophage infection and under artificial sputum medium and metal ion stress, suggesting roles in environmental adaptation and host interaction. This study provides the first systematic overview of PE/PPE gene repertoire in Mab and lays the groundwork for elucidating their roles in intracellular survival, host interaction, and antimicrobial resistance.

research.abstract: IntroductionCongenital portosystemic shunts (CPSS) are rare vascular malformations, with an estimated prevalence of 1/30000 live births, that cause portal blood to partly bypass the liver. CPSS frequently co-occur with congenital heart disease and other malformations, suggesting a shared developmental or genetic basis. Severe acquired clinical manifestations are present in a large proportion of patients with CPSS. Portopulmonary hypertension (PoPH), the most life-threatening, has been reported in as many as 7-14% of CPSS patients. Mounting evidence indicates that PoPH can arise early in life, particularly in children with CPSS, yet paediatric PoPH remains understudied. This project aims to identify genetic variants associated with PoPH in CPSS patients through whole-genomes, focusing primarily on known pathogenic genes for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), congenital heart disease (CHD), Hereditary Haemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT), SNPs previously associated with PoPH in adults, and ultimately novel genomic variants. The overarching goal of the study is to improve personalised risk assessment and inform clinical decisions regarding elective shunt closure in individuals potentially at-risk of developing PoPH. Methods and analysisThe aim is to perform an international multi-centre exploratory genome analysis of patients with CPSS and PoPH identified through the International Registry of Congenital Portosystemic Shunts (IRCPSS). Whole-genome sequencing will be utilized to analyse both coding and non-coding regions in a predominantly paediatric cohort. Targeted analysis of established pathogenic genes associated with PAH, CHD, HHT, and PoPH will be complemented by a genome-wide approach to identify novel, potentially pathogenic variants, with variant classification assessed according to American College of Medical Genetics (ACMG) criteria. Family-based analyses, including trio analyses and segregation studies, will enable the identification of dominant, recessive, and de novo variants, facilitating a comprehensive evaluation of variant inheritance pattern and pathogenic potential. Ethics and disseminationThis study has been approved by the CCER (Geneva cantonal ethics committee for research) and poses minimal risk to participants, limited to blood sampling performed as part of routine clinical care for patients. Genetic data will be securely stored and analysed in compliance with GDPR. Clinically significant findings will be communicated through recruiting physicians, in accordance with participant preference regarding incidental findings. Study results will be disseminated through open-access peer-reviewed publications and scientific conferences to advance understanding and management of PoPH in individuals with CPSS and potentially other chronic liver diseases associated with portosystemic bypass. research.abstract: Abstract The ultraspeciose clade Otophysa — catfishes, carps, minnows, tetras, and their kin — accounts for most vertebrate diversity in modern freshwater ecosystems. However, a controversial assemblage of largely-fragmentary marine fossils has led some authors, most recently Liu et al., to advocate parallel freshwater invasions for this otherwise inland lineage. Here, we test this hypothesis under multiple sources of uncertainty. We provide the first phylogenetic analysis of the recently-named marine fossil genus † Sooinichthys , resolving it as sister to all modern otophysans. We also find that † Santanichthys , long treated as an early marine otophysan, lacks a Weberian apparatus and plausibly belongs outside Ostariophysi entirely. When increasing the taxon and marker sampling of Liu et al.’s genomic dataset, standardizing their ecological coding, accounting for alternative interpretations of important morphological characters, and applying a suite of biogeographic models, we find a marine origin in only 6 of 132 analyses, and only when enforcing fossil placements inconsistent with our own phylogenetic results. We contend that the parallel freshwater invasion hypothesis of otophysan diversification is an artifact of sparse taxon sampling, taphonomic biases, model selection errors, and fossil overinterpretation. The result is a cautionary case for inferences about the cradle of any ancient freshwater clade.

research.abstract: Abstract This perspective provides an overview of what we know from real-world data on reversal of drug resistance evolution. An important question for those who study drug resistance is whether it is possible to reverse the evolution of resistance, for example by halting the use of specific drugs for a patient or even a community or country. Evidence for successful reversal of resistance levels is spread out in many different subfields of infectious disease. I use examples from P. falciparum malaria, several bacterial species including E. coli, M. tuberculosis, and S. aureus, and the viral pathogen HIV, to show that it is possible to reverse the evolution of resistance.

research.abstract: Abstract Cefiderocol is a siderophore-conjugated cephalosporin used to treat severe multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections. Its recent prioritisation for US national preparedness underscores its clinical importance, yet resistance can emerge despite apparent in vitro susceptibility. Here, we identify two regulatory routes to cefiderocol resistance in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB): mutation of the cAMP-producing adenylate cyclase CavA and truncation of the glycine-rich RNA-binding domain of the post-transcriptional regulator Hfq. These variants occurred in contemporary clinical isolates, conferred resistance in a murine CRAB lung-infection model and imposed minimal fitness costs. In Escherichia coli , deletion of the CavA orthologue cyaA increased competitive fitness during sub-inhibitory cefiderocol exposure. Hfq-CLASH and integrated omics revealed Hfq-dependent regulation of Fur-associated iron homeostasis in A. baumannii. Under iron limitation, truncated-Hfq induced a defence-primed state that attenuated siderophore uptake and reduced cefiderocol activity. These findings identify bacterial regulatory state and iron availability as determinants of cefiderocol susceptibility, with implications for resistance surveillance and susceptibility testing.

research.abstract: Abstract Tuberculosis, an infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis , remains endemic in regions where it is prevalent. Mycobacterium tuberculosis is an intracellular pathogen that can survive within host macrophages; however, the mechanisms governing its long-term persistence and the progression to active pulmonary tuberculosis remain poorly understood. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have been implicated in the initiation and progression of numerous diseases. In our previous study, circRNA sequencing identified several circRNAs associated with tuberculosis progression. In the present study, sequencing and reverse transcription–polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) analyses revealed that Circ_0074371 was significantly downregulated in monocytes from patients with active pulmonary tuberculosis (ATB) and was closely associated with disease onset and progression, exhibiting considerable diagnostic value for ATB. Functional experiments further showed that Circ_0074371 significantly impaired the intracellular survival of Mtb and promoted M1 macrophage polarization. Mechanistically, Circ_0074371 acted as a competing endogenous RNA by sequestering miR-4738-3p, a potent negative regulator of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) activation. Collectively, these findings identify Circ_0074371 as a tuberculosis-associated circRNA that regulates AMPK activity and reveal a novel mechanism through which Circ_0074371 influences macrophage polarization via the AMPK pathway, providing new insights into potential therapeutic targets for ATB.

research.abstract: Characium and Characium -like algae represent a taxonomically challenging group within Chlorophyceae. Due to their high phenotypic plasticity and convergent morphology, their true evolutionary relationships have long remained unresolved, and the lack of genomic resources has further hindered taxonomic revision. We sequenced and assembled seven complete chloroplast genomes from Characium and morphologically similar taxa and documented their detailed cell morphology. Comparative genomic analyses revealed that while most genomes retained the typical quadripartite structure, they exhibited significant structural variation, including gene rearrangements and diverse IR expansions/contractions. Furthermore, phylogenetic analyses based on 64 protein-coding genes successfully resolved the long-standing taxonomic ambiguity of Characium and Characium -like algae, placing the strains into three distinct, well-supported clades within Sphaeropleales and Volvocales. The synteny patterns and DCJ distances were consistent with the phylogeny: closely related species showed largely conserved gene order and low DCJ distances, whereas more distant lineages exhibited extensive rearrangements and higher distances. Branch-site tests identified a small set of positively selected genes, mainly related to photosynthesis, proteolysis, and plastid gene expression, suggesting that adaptive processes may have contributed to chloroplast genome diversity in these algae. This study establishes the first clear phylogenomic framework for these lineages, revealing distinct evolutionary patterns of gene loss and structural rearrangement that align with the newly resolved clades. It also provides an important basis for advancing studies on chloroplast genome evolution within Chlorophyceae.

research.abstract: Zoantharians (Cnidaria) are globally distributed from shallow reefs to the deep sea, yet their genomic resources remain scarce. Within the zoantharian genus Palythoa, most species harbor photosymbiotic dinoflagellates, whereas some have secondarily lost this symbiosis, allowing genomic changes associated with symbiotic status to be examined. Palythoa is also the original source of palytoxin, one of the most potent marine toxins known, but whether it is produced by the host or by associated microorganisms remains unresolved. Here we generated high-quality genome assemblies of two zooxanthellate Palythoa species and compared five Palythoa genomes spanning both symbiotic states with those of other anthozoans. Across anthozoans, genome size scaled with transposable element content, particularly retrotransposons. The azooxanthellate lineage carries substitutions in conserved domains of the symbiosis-related proteins LePin and NPC2 and shows rapid evolution of the lectin gene CLEC4A, whereas NF-{kappa}B and V-type H+-ATPase remain conserved. Palythoa genomes showed no lineage-specific expansion of polyketide synthase (PKS) genes; cnidarian PKS genes were restricted to P. caribaeorum and P. sp. sakurajimensis (clade III). In contrast, 27 bacterial PKS sequences were recovered from metatranscriptomes and a metagenome-assembled genome across species, including an azooxanthellate species, indicating that they derive from associated bacterial rather than Symbiodiniaceae. These genomes provide a comparative framework for zoantharians and reveal genomic changes associated with symbiotic status. We propose that palytoxin originates from associated bacteria rather than from the host, a hypothesis that can be tested by identifying the producing bacteria and their biosynthetic gene clusters.
